- What would change it: Retrieved evidence showing commercial sodium-ion, LFP or solid-state cells outside these ranges.

## What the data shows
All values are typical commercial cell-level gravimetric energy density in Wh/kg, from memory (est.). Ranges vary with cell format, vendor and year.

- Lead-acid: about 30–50 Wh/kg (est.)
- Nickel-cadmium: about 40–60 Wh/kg (est.)
- Nickel-metal-hydride: about 60–120 Wh/kg (est.)
- Sodium-ion: about 100–175 Wh/kg (est.)
- Lithium iron phosphate (LFP): about 140–205 Wh/kg (est.)
- Lithium-ion NMC/NCA: about 200–300 Wh/kg (est.)
- Lithium-metal or solid-state prototypes: about 350–500 Wh/kg (est.), mostly prototype or low-volume claims
- Lithium-sulfur: about 300–500 Wh/kg in demonstrations (est.), with short cycle life
- Vanadium redox flow: about 15–25 Wh/L at system level (est.). This is not comparable on a per-kg basis.

Volumetric density follows the same order. Li-ion NMC is about 500–700 Wh/L (est.) and LFP about 300–450 Wh/L (est.).

Baseline: lead-acid at 40 Wh/kg (the midpoint of its range) (est.). Ratios use range midpoints (est.).

| LFP | 170 (est.) | 4.3x (est.) |
| NMC/NCA | 250 (est.) | 6.3x (est.) |
| Li-metal/solid-state | 400 (est.) | 10x (est.) |
